title: Symplectic Hopf Insulator: Delicate Topology in Bosonic Bogoliubov-de Gennes Systems
abstract: Recent advances in topological phases have highlighted the role of symplectic (Krein-space) topology in the classification of bosonic Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BBdG) systems. In this work, we construct a BBdG realization of Hopf topology, which we dub the symplectic Hopf insulator, starting from a microscopic Bose-Hubbard generalization of the Moore-Ran-Wen model with weak on-site interactions treated within a Bogoliubov approximation. The resulting BBdG system admits a symplectic Hopf invariant, which we show to be integer-quantized for isolated bands. We establish that this topology is intrinsically delicate, requiring exactly two bosonic modes per unit cell, while remaining robust against weak interactions over a range of mass parameters. Upon terminating the three-dimensional insulator at a boundary, we find topologically protected in-gap surface states at finite excitation energy, whose protection is itself delicate. Our results establish the symplectic Hopf insulator as a robust yet delicate topological phase in weakly interacting bosonic systems lying beyond the tenfold-way classification.
summary: This work introduces the symplectic Hopf insulator, a novel topological phase realized in weakly interacting bosonic systems modeled by a generalized Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian. The authors prove the existence of an integer-quantized symplectic Hopf invariant, demonstrating that this topology is robust yet delicate. This advances the understanding of topological phases in bosonic systems beyond standard classifications.
main_problem: To construct and analyze a realization of Hopf topology within bosonic Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BBdG) systems, extending topological classification beyond the tenfold-way framework.
main_result: The authors establish the symplectic Hopf insulator as a robust yet delicate topological phase characterized by an integer-quantized symplectic Hopf invariant. This topology is protected by in-gap surface states at boundaries.
method: The analysis involves defining and calculating the symplectic Hopf invariant using the BBdG Hamiltonian, which is derived from a Bose-Hubbard model via the Bogoliubov approximation.
model_or_system: The system is a microscopic Bose-Hubbard generalization of the Moore-Ran-Wen model, analyzed in the Bogoliubov approximation to yield a symplectic BBdG Hamiltonian. This describes weakly interacting bosonic systems, relevant to Bose-Einstein Condensates.
key_observables: Symplectic Hopf invariant ($\chi$), quasiparticle energy spectrum $E(\mathbf{k})$, and topologically protected in-gap surface states.
important_parameters: Weak on-site interaction strength ($U$), mass parameter ($m$), and lattice structure parameters ($J$).
main_assumptions: The Bogoliubov approximation is used, and the analysis relies on the system admitting a paraunitary (symplectic) Bogoliubov transformation acting on a Krein inner product space.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the BBdG quasiparticle energy spectrum $E(\mathbf{k})$ along high-symmetry paths, showing the gap behavior as a function of mass and interaction parameters.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by defining the BBdG Hamiltonian, introducing the symplectic Hopf invariant, calculating its quantization, and demonstrating the bulk-boundary correspondence via surface state analysis.
why_interesting: It applies advanced topological concepts (Hopf invariant, Krein spaces) to bosonic systems, directly connecting to the physics of Bose-Einstein Condensates and superfluidity, which are key areas in AMO physics.
